text: The legacy criteria AC1 to AC12 of RWB-E2-021 stay with RWB-P6-E2021-APP (rwb-comms); this rwb-case slice writes nine new criteria under D-RCV-60 that test only the hold flag, the timeline facts and the NOTICE_UNSERVED task.
why: The WP fixes an empty acs list for a secondary split story, and the legacy criteria test the conduct check, the WIN file and the notice state, which rwb-case does not build.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 7; WP B2-P3-007 story line
impact: No legacy criterion is lost: it is owned once, by the rwb-comms story of the same legacy key.

text: The NOTICE_UNSERVED task carries the case owner role from LOV-ROLE, the task code NOTICE_UNSERVED and a due date read from the SERVICE_LEVEL reference row of rwb-case; no date or role is set in code.
why: The legacy story says the case goes to its owner's queue with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED and names no task code, role or due date.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 4 and 15; FSD P3 A2.11; TSD P3 T3.2 LOV-ROLE
impact: The task exists and is due; the due date moves with the reference row and not with a release.

text: This slice has no feature flag of its own; it is switched with the platform flag mechanism and the P6 dispatch-loop flag rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop, until a key is allocated in the parameter catalog.
why: The legacy story names only the P6 flag, and the FSD P3 feature list names no case-side key.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 13; FSD P3 A2.26
impact: An environment can turn the case side off with the loop; a separate key is a later parameter row, not a code change.

text: The ledger and the decision record are reached over the published rwb-source-data and rwb-decision REST contracts, on the R4 bases /api/recovery/source-data/v1 and /api/recovery/decision/v1, and every test uses their fakes rather than a live service.
why: The legacy story calls the two in-process interfaces and the split replaces them with REST contracts; neither operation name appears in the sources read for this WP.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12; Template and Rules R4 and DP-11
impact: The story builds and tests before the two contracts are live; only the paths change if the published contract differs.

text: The interaction ledger is owned by rwb-source-data under DP-18 and the R-PREC default ruling; rwb-case holds no interaction table, no view over it and no foreign key to it, and the TSD P3 T3.1 listing is superseded for the split.
why: The TSD lists interaction as a P3 object while the ownership rows of the context pack omit it; source precedence puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the TSD.
read: TSD P3 T3.1; context pack P3 ownership rows; Template and Rules R3 and DP-18
impact: One ledger, one owner, and a case timeline read that costs one hop instead of a cross-schema join.

text: A legal hold is placed and lifted with a reason from a hold reason list held as reference data of rwb-case, loaded and versioned by RW-COE without a code release; until the list is approved the reason is stored as it is given.
why: The legacy story cites R-UNI-20 and R-UNI-21 and gives no reason list, and the TSD P3 lists of values carry none.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 5 and 10; TSD P3 T3.2
impact: The hold works from Day 1; the reason codes arrive as a data load, not as a defect.

text: The platform contract stories that DP-03, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 name (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the reference-data contract of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, wave 1) are in place before Day 1 and are not repeated as H rows of this wave-2 story; the metadata rows carry only RWB-P6-E2021-CON.
why: The DP table adds H edges to platform CON stories while the WP fixes H empty for this story and the lane is Day 1 on CON dependencies only.
read: Template and Rules R5.5 and R5.7; WP B2-P3-007 story line
impact: The lane starts on Day 1; if a platform CON story slips, this story builds against its fake and the H edge is added by the planner.

why: Cited by _work/msr/editlog/B2-P3-007.md; see the story body for the default used.
